description: Tick-scaled block-parking (automatic unparking) and finalization (rolling checkpoints) vectors, mirroring validation.cpp's FindMostWorkChain and FindBlockToFinalize structures. Parking: requiredWork = tipChainWork + penalty, accepted iff the competing tip's chainwork strictly exceeds requiredWork; penalty P = D * clamp(tickDepth, 600, 2400)^2 / 5,760,000 with the quotient floored, where D = tipChainWork - forkChainWork and tickDepth is the divergence depth in ticks on the defending branch's schedule. The rule reads only (D, tickDepth), so the vectors carry the fork's chainwork (which cancels), the defender's span work and the competitor's span work directly, and heights only serve to derive the tick depth through a schedule. No block's work is computed and no nBits value is used. Equivalently, P = D/16 below 600 ticks, P = D * tickDepth^2 / 5,760,000 from 600 up to 2400, and P = D from 2400 onward. penaltyNum/penaltyDen express P as D*num/den with the quotient floored, and slackVsThreshold pins competingWorkSinceFork - (D + penalty): the vectors that sit on the threshold use 0 to reject (pinning the strict >) and 1 to accept, while vectors that deliberately sit away from it pin their margin. The penalty_depth* vectors use the never-activated `empty` schedule, so they pin the penalty function only: a chain-level verdict at those depths comes from the legacy arm, which would flip penalty_depth1_accept and penalty_depth3_reject. A span may straddle a schedule entry, including the activation boundary, as long as H_a + 1 is part of the defending branch (height(def) >= H_a + 1); the legacy count-keyed penalty for a tip still at or below H_a (height(def) <= H_a) is out of scope here. Finalization: candidate is the shallowest block at >= 6,000 ticks burial; the walk finalizes the candidate if now >= receiveTime + delay (inclusive) else walks back one block at a time, stopping at the already-finalized block; receiveTime 0 means disk-loaded = aged. The finalization check runs only when a new block connects (the `tip` field); the node startup grace period is a caller precondition, not a vector. Chainwork uses arith_uint256; hex fields are 64-char big-endian.

parking.name: penalty_depth1_reject
parking.note: d=600: P = D/16 = U/16. The legacy depth-1 tier was half a block; the ramp deliberately differs, and depth 1 is never parked anyway (the trigger is block-count, depth >= 2), so this tier exists only so the ramp is defined and continuous at its own knee

parking.name: penalty_depth1_accept
parking.note: one unit above the ramp threshold. The legacy arm would need D + W/2 = 3U/2 at this depth and reject E = 1.0625U, so the accept pins the penalty function only

parking.name: penalty_depth2_reject
parking.note: d=1200: P = D/4 = U/2, reproducing the legacy depth-2 half-block exactly; E == D + P stays parked

parking.name: penalty_depth2_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: penalty_depth3_reject
parking.note: d=1800: P = 9D/16 = 1.6875 U. The legacy tier was one whole block, so the ramp is stronger here, and 1.6875 U clears the whole-block boundary that difficulty drift used to decide at this depth. The legacy arm would need D + W = 4U and accept E = 4.6875U, so the reject pins the penalty function only

parking.name: penalty_depth3_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: penalty_depth4_reject
parking.note: d=2400: P = D, the 2x rule; E == 2D stays parked

parking.name: penalty_depth4_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_depth2_floor_reject
parking.note: d=120, the shallowest depth the trigger parks: clamped, so P = D/16 = U/8. A tip pinned at the future-time limit carries ~2.9% less difficulty per block than baseline and can only walk its clock back ~5 minutes per block, so the widest durable gap two tips can hold is ~3%, below this 6.25% floor: the depth-2 tie stays settled by work

parking.name: t60_depth2_floor_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold: +6.25% per block clears it

parking.name: t60_depth11_reject
parking.note: d=660: P = 121D/1600 = 0.831875 U, still under one block, so a one-block lead clears it (see prop_first_whole_block_crossing). The continuous crossing P = W sits between this depth and the next, at d = 702

parking.name: t60_depth11_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_depth12_reject
parking.note: d=720: P = 9D/100 = 1.08 U, the first depth at which P > W, so a one-block lead stops sufficing here (r(d) = 0.09 has grown past 1/12)

parking.name: t60_depth12_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_depth15_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_quarter1200_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_depth30_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_cap2400_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: straddle_seam_reject
parking.note: fork 999, tip 1001: d = T(1001) - T(999) = 600,060 - 599,400 = 660, because block 1000 contributes 600 ticks and block 1001 contributes 60. Two 60-tick blocks would read 720 and two 600-tick blocks would read 1,200; the ramp must read neither. r(660) = 121/1600, so P = 435,600 at D = U, and E == D + P stays parked

parking.name: straddle_seam_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: straddle_interior_reject
parking.note: fork 998, tip 1002: d = 600,120 - 598,800 = 1,320, an interior straddle point; r = 121/400, so P = 1,742,400 at D = U

parking.name: straddle_interior_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: seam_first_ramp_block
parking.note: fork 1000, tip 1001: the first span whose defending tip is past the activation block, so the ramp applies; d = T(1001) - T(1000) = 60, clamped to the 600-tick floor, so P = D/16 = U/16. A tip at 1000 itself (H_a) still takes the legacy count-keyed arm and is out of scope here; that one block is what separates the two readings of the handover predicate

parking.name: seam_first_ramp_block_accept
parking.note: accept twin of seam_first_ramp_block, completing the file's on-threshold pair for the handover boundary: one unit above P = D/16 accepts, one unit below rejects

parking.name: same_count_3pct_rejected
parking.note: E/D = 1.03 per block, the widest durable differential two tips can hold on timestamps alone, against a 1.0625 requirement: rejected, and rejected at every depth, because r(d) only grows from here. The slack pin is E - (D + P) = -374,400, i.e. 3.25% of D short of the threshold

parking.name: same_count_floor_reject
parking.note: the exact threshold at the shallowest parked depth: +6.25% per block, i.e. 17/16, and no more is needed because both spans hold two blocks

parking.name: same_count_floor_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: same_count_9p5pct_accepted
parking.note: E/D = 1.095 per block against a 1.0625 requirement: accepted with 374,400 of slack, the mirror of the 3.25% rejection above and the second deliberately off-boundary vector

parking.name: short_span2_of_depth3_reject
parking.note: defender at depth 3, competitor holds 2 blocks. d = 180 is inside the flat floor band, so the requirement is (3/2) * 17/16 = 51/32, i.e. each competitor block must average ~59.4% more work than the defender's. Deeper shorter-chain shapes are cheaper, see below

parking.name: short_span2_of_depth3_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: short_span9_of_depth10_reject
parking.note: the cheapest shorter-chain shape: defender at depth 10 against a 9-block competitor needs E > 1.0625 D, i.e. (10/9) * 17/16 = 1.1806, or ~18.1% more work per competitor block

parking.name: short_span9_of_depth10_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: mixed300_quarter1200_reject
parking.note: d = T(105) - T(101) = 61,500 - 60,300 = 1,200 on a 300-tick segment: identical penalty and verdict to t60_quarter1200_reject at the same tick depth on a 60-tick schedule

parking.name: mixed300_quarter1200_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: knee_599_reject
parking.note: one tick below the floor: clamped to 600, P = D/16 = U/16

parking.name: knee_600_reject
parking.note: at the floor: same value as 599, so the clamp is continuous

parking.name: knee_601_reject
parking.note: one tick above the floor: unclamped, P = D * 601^2/5,760,000, strictly greater than D/16

parking.name: knee_2399_reject
parking.note: one tick below the cap: P = D * 2399^2/5,760,000, strictly less than D

parking.name: knee_2400_reject
parking.note: at the cap: P = D

parking.name: knee_2401_reject
parking.note: one tick past the cap: clamped, so P is still D and not the extrapolated D * 2401^2/5,760,000

parking.name: wide_span_reject
parking.note: D = 1.6e19: the intermediate D * 600^2 is around 2^82, well past 64 bits, and the penalty is still exactly D/16

parking.name: wide_span_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: odd_span_ramp_reject
parking.note: D not a multiple of the denominator and d off the anchors: P = floor(D * 49/576) = 730,752,113 (remainder 546), which pins the single floor after the multiply

parking.name: odd_span_ramp_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: base_huge_reject
parking.note: same spans and depth as t60_depth2_floor_reject with a huge base: same penalty, same verdict

parking.name: base_huge_odd_reject
parking.note: and with the base's low bit set, so the subtraction cannot be truncating anywhere

finalization.name: fin_legacy_depth10_aged
finalization.note: candidate = tip - 10 = block 100; everything disk-loaded and aged

finalization.name: fin_legacy_walkback
finalization.note: block 100 received 'now' so not aged; walk back to block 99 (aged)

finalization.name: fin_legacy_age_exact
finalization.note: now == receiveTime + delay is aged (>= is inclusive)

finalization.name: fin_legacy_age_one_short
finalization.note: one second short of the age gate walks back instead

finalization.name: fin_legacy_already_finalized
finalization.note: candidate 100 is already finalized; the walk stops; blocks below are disk-loaded and aged, so walking past would have finalized 99

finalization.name: fin_legacy_none_aged
finalization.note: candidate 10 and every block below it received 'now'; walk terminates at genesis with nothing

finalization.name: fin_t60_depth100_aged
finalization.note: tip 1150: candidate = 100 one-minute blocks back = block 1050

finalization.name: fin_t60_straddle_activation
finalization.note: T(1100) - 6000 = 600,000 = T(1000): candidate is the activation block

finalization.name: fin_t60_candidate_preactivation
finalization.note: T(1090) - 6000 = 599,400 = T(999): candidate sits below activation

finalization.name: fin_t60_walkback_cross_activation
finalization.note: candidate 1000 (activation block) not aged; walk back to pre-activation block 999

finalization.name: fin_mixed_mid600
finalization.note: T(101)=60,300; block 91 is only 5,700 ticks deep, so candidate is block 90 (6,300 deep)

finalization.name: fin_mixed_300region
finalization.note: 20 blocks of 300 ticks = 6,000 ticks: candidate = block 120

finalization.name: fin_legacy_short_chain
finalization.note: T(5) = 3,000 < 6,000: chain shallower than the depth gate has no candidate (legacy GetAncestor returns nullptr); nothing finalizes even though every block is disk-loaded and aged
